topic: Designing stable ProblemDetail types instead of parsing error messages
tomorrowTopic: Mapping domain failures to HTTP status without coupling domain code to Spring

hook.headline: Machines need identities, not prose
hook.hook: If a React client branches on an error message, a wording change can become a breaking API change. Give the problem a stable machine-readable identity and keep explanatory text for humans.
hook.visualCaption: stable problem type → client decision; mutable detail → human guidance
hook.microExample: email-taken stays stable while detail text can improve

mentalModel.title: Separate error identity from explanation
mentalModel.coreIdea: In RFC 9457 Problem Details, type identifies the problem kind, while detail explains this occurrence for a human. Clients should branch on documented machine-readable semantics, not parse detail text.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Error wording can evolve without silently changing the client's decision logic.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: type drives code; detail helps people

code.title: Make the problem type the contract
code.intro: A conflict can carry a documented type URI plus human-readable text.
code.code:
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/email-taken",
  "title": "Email already registered",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "Choose a different email address."
}
code.highlightReason: RFC 9457 defines type as the primary identifier for the problem type; this is the field machine consumers should treat as semantic identity.
code.takeaway: Do not make client control flow depend on detail text.
code.professionalNote: A type URI should have stable, documented semantics. It can be dereferenceable documentation, but clients should not need to fetch it at runtime to understand the response.

production.title: Avoid accidental contracts in prose
production.scenario: A React signup form checks whether detail contains "already exists" before showing an email-specific recovery path.
problems: Copy edits or localization can break the branch.
Different endpoints may describe the same failure differently.
Raw exception messages can leak implementation detail and are poor public contracts.
production.professionalApproach: Define a small set of documented problem types, map application failures to appropriate HTTP semantics at the web boundary, let clients branch on the stable type, and treat title/detail as human-facing text.
production.debugClue: If the UI falls back to a generic error, inspect the returned type first; do not start by matching a new detail string.

interview.question: Why should an API client not branch on the ProblemDetail detail field?
interview.answer: Because detail is human-readable, occurrence-specific text and RFC 9457 says consumers should not parse it for information. Use a documented machine-readable problem identity such as type for control flow, keep the HTTP status semantically correct, and reserve detail for guidance that may change or be localized.
remember: type is the primary problem-type identifier
detail is human-readable and should not drive parsing logic
HTTP status still carries generic protocol semantics
